text:
Noah: Quick question — I had a multi-city trip for work but added two personal days at the end. I used my personal card for a couple of rides (Lyft/rail), and the hotel charged one combined invoice for the whole stay. Can I still claim the business portion?
Ava (People Ops): Yes, you can. Short answer: submit only the business nights and business transport, attach receipts and evidence of the business trip (calendar invite or flight itinerary).
Noah: For the hotel invoice (single invoice for 6 nights, 4 business + 2 personal), do I need the hotel to reissue a split invoice or can I submit one and note the business nights?
Ava (People Ops): Prefer reissue if possible — it speeds review and VAT reclaim. If they can’t, submit the single invoice plus a short note and your calendar/itinerary showing the business dates. Also include a calculation: how much to reimburse (rate per night * business nights).
Noah: Got it. And rides — I split a Lyft with a teammate and paid my portion. Do I submit my share? How do I annotate?
Maya: I do split rides all the time. Submit your actual charged amount and upload the ride receipt screenshot. Add in the notes who was on the ride and the business purpose.
Ava (People Ops): Exactly. For split payments, expense the exact amount you paid. If the receipt shows the full fare, include a screenshot of your card statement or the in-app payment confirmation showing your charged amount.
Noah: What about per diem? Breakfast was provided by the conference on one day. Do I still claim per diem for that day?
Ava (People Ops): If a meal is provided at the conference, reduce the meal portion of per diem for that day. Our policy: per diem is pro-rated if employer provides any meals. So submit per diem for the remainder or submit meal receipts if you prefer itemized.
Devon: FYI — for EU trips remember to upload VAT invoices. Finance can reclaim where allowed.
Sam (Finance): Yup. VAT: upload the original invoice (not a credit card receipt). If the supplier won't provide VAT details, note that in the expense and Finance will advise. Also tell us the currency; we convert using the midday rate on the date of transaction unless you provide a bank/FX fee showing a different rate.
Noah: Example of how to fill the expense system?
Ava (People Ops): Submit separate line items so reviewers can quickly approve. Example (one expense with 3 line items):
```
Line 1: Hotel — Business nights only
  Amount: 320.00 EUR
  Currency: EUR
  Notes: Business nights 2026-05-10 to 2026-05-13 (attach calendar + full invoice)
Line 2: Lyft — airport to hotel (my share)
  Amount: 18.75 EUR
  Currency: EUR
  Notes: Screenshot of Lyft receipt + card charge
Line 3: Per diem — conference days (reduced for provided breakfast)
  Amount: 24.00 EUR
  Currency: EUR
  Notes: Conference provided breakfast on 2026-05-12
```
Ava (People Ops): Attach the full hotel invoice, then in the notes show the calculation you used to extract the business portion (e.g., 4 nights x 80 EUR/night = 320 EUR).
Noah: What about currency conversion? My card statement shows USD charge — but receipt is in EUR. Do I need to enter USD?
Sam (Finance): Enter the original currency and amount (EUR) and attach the card statement showing the USD charge. We’ll validate and use the policy rate or the card rate per policy. If you paid FX fees, attach that too.
Maya: If the supplier refuses to split the invoice, I always email them and CC Finance; sometimes mentioning VAT reclaim makes them reissue faster.
Noah: Any special case for personal extension nights where company paid the whole invoice and I reimburse them?
Ava (People Ops): If company card was used for whole stay and you want to reimburse the personal portion, ask Finance for a private-pay link OR create an expense with negative line item for reimbursement and attach proof of payment. Better: easiest is to reimburse via the private-pay portal or ask Finance to process chargeback to your card.
Devon: ExpenseBot reminder: do not combine personal and business charges into one line item. Separate them. :white_check_mark:
Noah: Thanks! Where can I find the step-by-step doc?
Ava (People Ops): See our travel & expenses wiki (People Ops > Travel > Multi-leg trips). If you want, DM me the receipts and I can check before you submit. :+1:
